cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:1-3), gets another word from the LORD. God tells him, 'Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her abominations…' Buckle up, friend, because this one's heavy and God starts it at the very beginning.

cards.question: God goes all the way back to Jerusalem's beginning. He says her origin and birth were in the land of the ___.

cards.text: God says her father was an Amorite and her mother a Hittite, two peoples who lived in Canaan.
Then God takes us back to the day Jerusalem was born. A newborn should get her cord cut, a wash, a rub with salt and some cloths to be wrapped in.

cards.question: Cut the cord, wash her, rub her with salt, wrap her in cloths. How many of those things does anyone do for newborn Jerusalem?
With no one to care for her, newborn Jerusalem is thrown out into the open field.

cards.text: Despised on the day she was born, she's left out there alone. Then God passes by and sees her lying in her blood.

cards.question: God sees baby Jerusalem lying in her blood in the open field. What does He do?

answers.text: He sends her back to her parents

cards.text: 'Live!' God says it twice. Then He makes her thrive like a plant of the field, and she grows up very beautiful.

cards.question: Grown up and very beautiful, Jerusalem is dressed in fine clothes by now.

cards.text: She's still 'naked and bare.' Then God passes by again, sees she's old enough for love, and spreads His cloak over her.

cards.question: God pledges Himself to Jerusalem and enters into a ___ with her, and she becomes His.

cards.text: He bathes her, rinses off her blood, and dresses her in embroidered cloth, fine linen and silk. Me? One hat, one neckerchief, one APRON.

cards.question: After the bracelets, the chain, the nose ring and the earrings, what does God put on Jerusalem's head?

cards.text: Dressed in gold and silver and eating fine flour, honey and oil, the baby from the open field rises to be queen. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, and the only thing that went up back there was the DUST pile.

cards.question: Queen Jerusalem's beauty stays a secret that only God knows about.
Jerusalem's fame spreads among the nations because her beauty is perfect. Where does that perfect beauty come from?

cards.text: But this is where the story turns, friend. God says that because of her fame, Jerusalem starts trusting in something.

cards.question: Because of her fame, Queen Jerusalem starts trusting in her own beauty.

cards.text: She plays the harlot, and her beauty is there for anyone who passes by. She even takes some of the clothes God gave her and makes colorful high places for herself.

cards.question: Jerusalem takes the gold and silver jewelry God gave her and makes ___ out of it.

cards.text: She drapes her embroidered garments over those idols. Then she sets God's oil and incense in front of them.

cards.question: Even the fine flour, oil and honey God fed Jerusalem ends up set before her idols.

cards.text: Then she goes even further. She takes the sons and daughters she bore to God and sacrifices them as food to idols, and God calls them 'My children'.

cards.question: Through all her abominations, what does God say Jerusalem never remembered?

answers.text: The days when she lay in her blood
The songs she sang as a queen
The names of all her neighbors

cards.text: Then God says, 'Woe! Woe to you…' On top of all her other wickedness, she builds herself a mound and a lofty shrine.

cards.question: Jerusalem keeps her mounds and lofty shrines tucked away where nobody can see them.

cards.text: She builds them in every public square and at the head of every street, and she degrades her beauty with increasing promiscuity. Then she turns to her lustful neighbors.

cards.question: Which of Jerusalem's neighbors does God name first as her lovers?

cards.text: God says she did it to provoke Him to anger, so He stretches out His hand against her and reduces her portion. He gives her over to those who hate her, the daughters of the Philistines.

cards.question: The daughters of the Philistines are impressed by Jerusalem's lewd conduct.

cards.text: Egypt wasn't enough, so she turns to the Assyrians. And she's STILL not satisfied.

cards.question: After Egypt and Assyria, Jerusalem turns to Chaldea, the land of merchants. How does that go?

cards.text: 'How weak-willed is your heart,' God says. He calls her an adulterous wife who takes in strangers instead of her own husband.

cards.question: In God's picture, prostitutes get paid. What does He say Jerusalem does instead?

answers.text: She pays her lovers to come to her
She demands gold and silver from them
She sends every one of them away

cards.text: Then comes the call: 'Therefore, O prostitute, hear the word of the LORD!' God says she poured out her wealth and exposed her nakedness to her lovers and all her detestable idols.

cards.question: God names one more reason judgment is coming on Jerusalem. What is it?

cards.text: So God says He'll gather a crowd against her from all around.

cards.question: Who does God say He'll gather against Jerusalem?

cards.text: That's all those she loved and all those she hated, and He'll expose her before them. Then God names her sentence.

cards.question: God sentences Jerusalem to the punishment of women who commit adultery and those who shed blood.

cards.text: Then God says He'll hand her over to those very same lovers.

cards.question: What does God say Jerusalem's lovers will do to the mounds and lofty shrines she built?

cards.text: God says they'll strip off her clothes, take her fine jewelry and leave her naked and bare. That's the same 'naked and bare' she was before God ever clothed her.
God says a mob will come against her, stone her and cut her to pieces with their swords. They'll burn down her houses too.

cards.question: God says His judgment against Jerusalem will be carried out in secret, where no one can see.
God says He'll put an end to Jerusalem's prostitution, and she will never again ___ her lovers.
After all this judgment, God says He'll stay angry with Jerusalem forever.

cards.text: Because she did not remember the days of her youth, God says He'll bring her deeds down upon her own head. Hold that thought, friend, because God still has more to say to Jerusalem.
